concepts.heading: The Habit Loop: Your Blueprint for Change
concepts.alt: A guide pointing at a circular loop of arrows with three icons: a bell, footprints and a star
concepts.plain: Every habit is a loop: something sets it off, you do it, you get a payoff.

concepts.heading: The Science: How Long Does Habit Formation Actually Take?
concepts.alt: A guide marking days on a long wall calendar
concepts.plain: The 21-day claim is a myth. Building a habit usually takes longer.

concepts.heading: Growth Mindset: The Foundation
concepts.alt: A guide watering a small plant growing out of an open book
concepts.plain: A growth mindset means believing you can get better with effort.

checks.after: The Habit Loop: Your Blueprint for Change
checks.prompt: What are the three parts of the habit loop?
checks.explanation: Cue, routine, reward. Every action follows the same habit loop: a cue, a routine and a reward.

checks.prompt: A growth mindset is the belief that…
options: Abilities can be developed with effort
checks.explanation: Abilities can be developed with effort. Carol Dweck's research at Stanford showed how mindset affects achievement and resilience.

caec718d-6e5a-4ab9-b9c3-a8f4f3de535f.takeaway: Every habit runs on a loop: a cue, a routine and a reward. Change the loop and you change the habit.

concepts.heading: The 1% Better Every Day Principle
concepts.alt: A guide climbing a long staircase made of very small steps
concepts.plain: Getting a tiny bit better each day adds up to a lot.

concepts.heading: Identity-Based Habits: The Real Leverage
concepts.alt: A guide looking into a mirror where her reflection wears a small medal
concepts.plain: Habits stick when they come from who you are, not just from a goal.

concepts.heading: Mapping Your Personal Habit Landscape
concepts.alt: A guide drawing a map with a pencil, with a small house, a heart and a briefcase on it
concepts.plain: Before you change anything, look clearly at what you do now.

checks.prompt: What is the "1% better every day" idea?
options: Small improvements build momentum over time
checks.explanation: Small improvements build momentum over time. A growth mindset creates momentum, and small daily gains build on each other.

checks.prompt: Which habits give the real leverage?
checks.explanation: Identity-based habits. Goal-based habits aim at an outside target. Identity-based habits come from who you believe you are.

adf192f6-9ccd-4ab9-93a4-c48be9967a09.takeaway: Small daily improvements add up, and they stick best when they match who you want to be.

concepts.heading: The Power of Implementation Intentions
concepts.alt: A guide pinning a note with a clock and a map pin onto a board
concepts.plain: Decide exactly when and where you will do it. That makes you far more likely to follow through.

concepts.heading: The Neuroscience: Habits as Automatic Behavior
concepts.alt: A guide strolling on autopilot along a worn footpath in the grass
concepts.plain: Almost half of what we do each day is automatic habit.

concepts.heading: The Four Laws of Behavior Change
concepts.alt: A guide holding four coloured cards fanned out
concepts.plain: Four rules make any habit easier to build.

concepts.heading: 1. Make It Obvious: Environmental Design
concepts.alt: A guide placing running shoes right beside the front door
concepts.plain: Make it obvious: set up your space so the right thing is in plain sight.

concepts.heading: 2. Make It Attractive: Pair With Joy
concepts.alt: Two guides dancing together while washing dishes
concepts.plain: Make it attractive: pair it with something you enjoy.

concepts.heading: 3. Make It Easy: Reduce Friction
concepts.alt: A guide stepping easily over a very low hurdle
concepts.plain: Make it easy: start with a version that takes two minutes.

concepts.heading: 4. Make It Satisfying: Celebrate Wins
concepts.alt: A guide ticking a box on a wall chart and doing a small fist pump
concepts.plain: Make it satisfying: celebrate each small win straight away.

checks.after: The Neuroscience: Habits as Automatic Behavior
checks.prompt: About how much of our daily behaviour is habit?
checks.explanation: 43%. Wendy Wood's research shows that 43% of our daily behaviours are performed out of habit.

checks.prompt: Which tools make a habit easy?
options: Habit stacking and the two-minute rule
checks.explanation: Habit stacking and the two-minute rule. Use habit stacking and the two-minute rule to lower the barrier to entry.

daea0e4c-0fff-41bf-9727-7bd6bb6c79a0.takeaway: Make the habit obvious, attractive, easy and satisfying.

concepts.heading: Breaking Bad Patterns: Replace, Don't Resist
concepts.alt: A guide swapping a worn gear for a shiny new one in a small machine
concepts.plain: Bad habits once helped you. Swap them for something better instead of fighting them.

concepts.heading: The 2-Minute Identity Ritual
concepts.alt: Two guides facing each other, holding hands and taking a slow breath together
concepts.plain: Pick one two-minute practice and do it every day.

concepts.heading: Habit Stacking Across Life Domains
concepts.alt: A guide joining two chain links together
concepts.plain: Attach a new habit to something you already do, like right after dinner.

concepts.heading: Integration Across Life
concepts.plain: The same rules work in love, work, health and money.

checks.after: Breaking Bad Patterns: Replace, Don't Resist
checks.prompt: What is the advice for breaking a bad pattern?
checks.explanation: Replace it, don't resist it. Most unhealthy habits exist because they worked at some point. Your nervous system learned they delivered a reward—safety, control, distraction, pain relief, numbness, attention.

options: Linking a new habit to an existing one
checks.explanation: Linking a new habit to an existing one. Habit stacking links a new habit to one you already do, like sharing an appreciation right after dinner.

05c0c270-21ca-428f-8439-92f00472d416.takeaway: Do not fight a bad habit. Replace it, and attach new habits to ones you already have.

concepts.heading: Self-Image Formation: How Your Thermostat Gets Set
concepts.alt: A guide looking at a wall of sticky notes and peeling one off
concepts.plain: Your self-image was built from what you were told and what happened to you.

concepts.heading: The Success Mechanism vs. Failure Mechanism
concepts.alt: At a railway switch lever, choosing between two tracks
concepts.plain: Your mind runs in success mode or failure mode, depending on what you believe about yourself.

concepts.heading: Self-Acceptance and Physical Health
concepts.alt: A guide hugging herself with a calm smile
concepts.plain: Accepting yourself is linked to better well-being.

concepts.heading: Cultural Programming and Self-Image
concepts.alt: A guide walking away from a billboard that shows a perfect glowing silhouette
concepts.plain: Family, culture and media all shaped how you see yourself.

checks.after: Self-Image Formation: How Your Thermostat Gets Set
checks.explanation: Things like childhood messages. Self-image is built from things like childhood messaging.

checks.prompt: What did Carol Ryff's research study?
options: The link between self-acceptance and well-being
checks.explanation: The link between self-acceptance and well-being. Carol Ryff's psychological well-being research looked at self-acceptance.

3dc6aea5-0bd4-4984-89b1-86214b6561a5.takeaway: Your self-image was learned from early messages and experiences, so it can be relearned.

concepts.heading: The Power of Self-Affirmation Under Stress
concepts.alt: A guide holding a shield decorated with a heart and a star while light rain falls
concepts.plain: Reminding yourself of what you value helps you stay steady under stress.

concepts.heading: Releasing Protective Beliefs
concepts.alt: A guide taking off a heavy suit of armour and setting it down gently
concepts.plain: Most limiting beliefs began as protection. You can let them go when they are no longer needed.

concepts.heading: Identity Reframes: From Scarcity to Abundance
concepts.alt: A guide turning a card over from a grey side to a bright colourful side
concepts.plain: Rewrite the old story about yourself into one that is fair and true.

concepts.heading: From Scarcity to Abundance in Relationships
concepts.alt: A guide holding an overflowing basket of hearts and offering some
concepts.plain: Love is not a pie that runs out. There is enough.

checks.prompt: Why did most limiting self-images form?
checks.explanation: As protection. Most limiting self-images formed as protection. If a parent was emotionally unavailable, you learned "seeking connection is futile."

checks.after: From Scarcity to Abundance in Relationships
checks.prompt: A scarcity mindset in relationships says…
options: There isn't enough to go around
checks.explanation: There isn't enough to go around. Many people discover that a scarcity mindset, the fear that there isn't enough, is holding them back.

ee3be82c-2548-4f47-b255-1e61f221f8a9.takeaway: Old beliefs once protected you. Thank them, then replace them with ones that are true now.
